objects.description: Enumeration of supported audio sample formats used for input/output buffers in the C API.

objects.definition:
typedef enum {
#ifndef GGWAVE_CONFIG_FEW_PROTOCOLS
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_AUDIBLE_NORMAL,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_AUDIBLE_FAST,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_AUDIBLE_FASTEST,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_ULTRASOUND_NORMAL,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_ULTRASOUND_FAST,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_ULTRASOUND_FASTEST,
#endif
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_DT_NORMAL,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_DT_FAST,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_DT_FASTEST,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_MT_NORMAL,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_MT_FAST,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_MT_FASTEST,

#ifndef GGWAVE_CONFIG_FEW_PROTOCOLS
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_0,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_1,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_2,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_3,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_4,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_5,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_6,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_7,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_8,
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_CUSTOM_9,

#endif
        GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_COUNT,
    } ggwave_ProtocolId;
objects.description: Enumeration of all protocol identifiers supported by GGWave for transmission and reception, including audible, ultrasound, dual-tone (DT), and multi-tone (MT) variants.
Enumeration of filter kinds available to GGWave::filter for preprocessing or postprocessing waveforms.
Opaque instance identifier used by the C API to refer to an internal GGWave instance stored in a private map. Constructed via ggwave_init() and released with ggwave_free().

objects.definition:
typedef struct {
        int                 payloadLength;        // payload length
        float               sampleRateInp;        // capture sample rate
        float               sampleRateOut;        // playback sample rate
        float               sampleRate;           // the operating sample rate
        int                 samplesPerFrame;      // number of samples per audio frame
        float               soundMarkerThreshold; // sound marker detection threshold
        ggwave_SampleFormat sampleFormatInp;      // format of the captured audio samples
        ggwave_SampleFormat sampleFormatOut;      // format of the playback audio samples
        int                 operatingMode;        // operating mode
    } ggwave_Parameters;
objects.description: Configuration struct for creating or preparing a GGWave instance: sample rates, frame size, marker threshold, sample formats, fixed/variable payload length, and operating mode flags.

C++ class implementing GGWave signal generation and decoding, managing protocols, buffers, FFT/filter utilities, and a sinc-based resampler. Construct via default+prepare or parameterized ctor; lifetime managed by user code.
Protocol descriptor used by GGWave for both Tx and Rx: frequency layout, framing, payload sizing, mono/multi-tone flag, and enable state with helper metrics.
Container of Protocol descriptors for all protocol IDs with helpers to enable/disable and select subsets; provides default-initialized global sets for Tx and Rx.
Sinc-interpolation resampler used internally by GGWave. Provides buffer allocation via external heap, stateful streaming resample(), and parameters controlling sinc table density and delay line.

functions.name: ggwave_setLogFile
functions.description: Sets the FILE-like stream used by GGWave’s internal logging. Pass stderr/stdout or NULL to disable logging. Not thread-safe; intended for configuring library-wide logging before instances run.
requirements: fptr may be NULL to disable logging.
Not thread-safe: do not call while any GGWave instances are running.
Argument is a FILE* passed as void*; caller must ensure it points to a valid FILE when non-NULL.

functions.name: ggwave_getDefaultParameters
functions.description: Returns a ggwave_Parameters struct populated with default values suitable for typical use. Use as a baseline, then modify fields before initializing an instance.
requirements: No input arguments.
Returned struct is by value; caller may modify a copy freely.

functions.name: ggwave_init
functions.description: Creates and registers a new GGWave instance with the specified parameters and returns its opaque instance ID. Caller must free the instance with ggwave_free when done.
requirements: parameters fields should be set appropriately; use ggwave_getDefaultParameters() as a base.
Returned instance ID must be passed to other C APIs and eventually to ggwave_free().
At most GGWAVE_MAX_INSTANCES instances may be active (implied by header constant).

functions.name: ggwave_free
functions.description: Destroys and deregisters a GGWave instance created by ggwave_init, releasing its resources.
requirements: instance must be a valid instance ID previously returned by ggwave_init.
Do not use the instance after calling this function.

functions.name: ggwave_encode
functions.signature: GGWAVE_API int ggwave_encode(ggwave_Instance instance, const void * payloadBuffer, int payloadSize, ggwave_ProtocolId protocolId, int volume, void * waveformBuffer, int query);
functions.description: Encodes binary payload into an audio waveform using the specified protocol and volume. If query != 0, no encoding occurs and the function returns the required output size (in bytes if query==1, otherwise in samples). On success with query==0, returns number of generated bytes. Returns -1 on error.
requirements: instance must be a valid GGWave instance initialized for TX (operatingMode must allow TX).
payloadBuffer must point to payloadSize bytes when query==0; may be NULL if payloadSize==0 or only querying size.
payloadSize is the number of bytes to encode; must be non-negative.
protocolId must be a supported TX protocol for the instance (enabled at prepare/init time).
volume is in range [0, 100]; comment advises not going over 50, typical 25.
waveformBuffer must be large enough to hold the generated waveform when query==0; size in bytes is nSamples * sizeOfSample_bytes using sampleFormatOut.
If query != 0, waveformBuffer can be NULL; function reports required size (bytes if query==1, samples otherwise).
Returns -1 on error; caller should handle this as failure.

functions.name: ggwave_decode
functions.signature: GGWAVE_API int ggwave_decode(ggwave_Instance instance, const void * waveformBuffer, int waveformSize, void * payloadBuffer);
functions.description: Feeds captured audio waveform data to the decoder. Returns the number of decoded payload bytes if a payload is detected, 0 if none, or -1 on error (e.g., excessive noise). Decoded data written to payloadBuffer is not null-terminated.
requirements: instance must be a valid GGWave instance initialized for RX (operatingMode must allow RX).
waveformBuffer must point to waveformSize bytes of audio samples in the instance’s configured input sample format (sampleFormatInp).
payloadBuffer must be writable and large enough to hold up to GGWave::kMaxDataSize bytes; data is not null-terminated.
Call repeatedly with successive audio chunks, typically samplesPerFrame * sampleSize bytes per call (as shown in example).
Caller must check for return -1 (error) and >0 (bytes decoded).

functions.name: ggwave_ndecode
functions.signature: GGWAVE_API int ggwave_ndecode(ggwave_Instance instance, const void * waveformBuffer, int waveformSize, void * payloadBuffer, int payloadSize);
functions.description: Memory-safe variant of ggwave_decode that additionally takes the output buffer size. Returns number of decoded bytes, 0 if none, -1 on decode error, or -2 if payloadBuffer is too small.
requirements: instance must be a valid GGWave instance with RX enabled.
waveformBuffer must point to waveformSize bytes in the configured input sample format.
payloadBuffer must be writable; payloadSize must be its capacity in bytes.
Caller must handle -2 indicating insufficient output buffer size.

functions.name: ggwave_rxToggleProtocol
functions.signature: GGWAVE_API void ggwave_rxToggleProtocol(ggwave_ProtocolId protocolId, int state);
functions.description: Globally enable or disable an RX protocol for newly constructed GGWave instances. Does not affect already created instances.
requirements: protocolId must be a valid ggwave_ProtocolId.
state: 0 disables, 1 enables.
Effect applies only to future instances; existing instances are unaffected.

functions.name: ggwave_txToggleProtocol
functions.signature: GGWAVE_API void ggwave_txToggleProtocol(ggwave_ProtocolId protocolId, int state);
functions.description: Globally enable or disable a TX protocol for newly constructed GGWave instances. Does not affect already created instances.
requirements: protocolId must be a valid ggwave_ProtocolId.
state: 0 disables, 1 enables.
Effect applies only to future instances; existing instances are unaffected.

functions.name: ggwave_rxProtocolSetFreqStart
functions.description: Sets the starting FFT bin (freqStart) for a specific RX protocol. Adjusts the lowest tone frequency used by that protocol for receivers created after the change.
requirements: protocolId must be a valid RX protocol id.
freqStart is an integer FFT bin index; must be appropriate for the configured sample rate and FFT size.
Affects only newly created instances; existing instances are unaffected (by analogy with toggles).

functions.name: ggwave_txProtocolSetFreqStart
functions.description: Sets the starting FFT bin (freqStart) for a specific TX protocol. Adjusts the lowest tone frequency for transmitters created after the change.
requirements: protocolId must be a valid TX protocol id.
freqStart is an integer FFT bin index.
Affects only newly created instances; existing instances are unaffected (by analogy with toggles).

functions.name: ggwave_rxDurationFrames
functions.description: Returns the recvDuration_frames value for the RX state of the specified instance, i.e., expected receive duration in frames.
requirements: instance must be a valid GGWave instance.
Instance must have RX prepared for this value to be meaningful.

functions.name: GGWave::GGWave
functions.description: Default constructor for GGWave. Does not allocate memory or prepare the instance; prepare() must be called before encode/decode operations.
requirements: Caller must call prepare(parameters) before using encode/decode or other operations that require allocated buffers.

functions.name: GGWave::GGWave
functions.description: Constructs and prepares a GGWave instance with the given parameters. Equivalent to default-constructing then calling prepare(parameters).
requirements: parameters should be valid; typically obtained from GGWave::getDefaultParameters or ggwave_getDefaultParameters.
Construction may fail internally if parameters are invalid; behavior on failure not specified in header.

functions.name: GGWave::~GGWave
functions.description: Destructor for GGWave. Releases any resources allocated during prepare/encode/decode.
requirements: Object must not be used after destruction.

functions.name: GGWave::prepare
functions.signature: bool GGWave::prepare(const GGWave::Parameters & parameters, bool allocate = true);
functions.description: Allocates and initializes all internal buffers according to parameters and the currently enabled global protocols (Protocols::rx/tx). If allocate is false, it only computes required sizes without allocating. Must be called when using the default constructor.
requirements: Call only if the instance was default-constructed (do not call if you used the parameters constructor).
If allocate == false, do not use the instance for encode/decode; use heapSize() to inspect memory needs.
Enabled protocols in GGWave::Protocols::rx() and tx() should be configured before calling prepare for optimal memory usage.
Returns false if parameters are invalid or allocation/initialization fails (implied).

functions.name: GGWave::setLogFile
functions.description: Sets the FILE stream for GGWave’s internal logging at the C++ level. Pass nullptr to disable. Not thread-safe; do not call while any instances are running.
requirements: fptr may be nullptr to disable logging.
Not thread-safe: avoid calling while any GGWave instances are running.

functions.name: GGWave::getDefaultParameters
functions.description: Returns a reference to a static default-constructed parameters object containing recommended defaults.
requirements: Returned reference refers to static storage; do not free. Treat as read-only.

functions.name: GGWave::init
functions.signature: bool GGWave::init(const char * text, GGWave::TxProtocolId protocolId, const int volume = kDefaultVolume);
functions.description: Initializes the transmitter path with the given null-terminated text payload, protocol, and volume, preparing for a subsequent encode().
requirements: Instance must have been prepared with TX enabled.
text must be a valid null-terminated string pointer.
protocolId must be an enabled TX protocol for this instance.
volume is an integer; typical range is [0, 100] with low values recommended.

functions.name: GGWave::init
functions.signature: bool GGWave::init(int dataSize, const char * dataBuffer, GGWave::TxProtocolId protocolId, const int volume = kDefaultVolume);
functions.description: Initializes the transmitter path with a binary payload of size dataSize, protocol, and volume, preparing for a subsequent encode().
requirements: Instance must have been prepared with TX enabled.
dataBuffer must point to at least dataSize bytes; dataSize must be non-negative.
protocolId must be an enabled TX protocol for this instance.
volume is an integer; typical range is [0, 100] with low values recommended.

functions.name: GGWave::encodeSize_bytes
functions.description: Returns the expected size in bytes of the waveform that would be produced by encode(). When output sample rate differs from operating sample rate, this may overestimate.
requirements: Call after successful init(...) and prepare().
Value is an estimate and may be an overestimation when sampleRateOut != sampleRate.

functions.name: GGWave::encodeSize_samples
functions.description: Returns the expected waveform length in samples for the pending transmission. May overestimate when resampling is involved.
requirements: Call after successful init(...) and prepare().
Result may overestimate when sampleRateOut != sampleRate.

functions.name: GGWave::encode
functions.description: Encodes the initialized TX data into an audio waveform. Returns the number of bytes in the generated waveform. Access data via txWaveform() and txTones().
requirements: Instance must be prepared with TX enabled.
A prior successful init(...) must have been called to set the payload.
Caller should retrieve output via txWaveform() or tones via txTones() after calling.

functions.name: GGWave::decode
functions.signature: bool GGWave::decode(const void * data, uint32_t nBytes);
functions.description: Decodes an audio waveform buffer. Returns false if the waveform is invalid; otherwise updates RX state so the caller can query/take decoded data and analysis outputs.
requirements: Instance must be prepared with RX enabled.
data must point to nBytes of samples in the configured input sample format (sampleFormatInp()).
Caller should check RX state via rx* methods and retrieve data via rxTakeData or analysis via rxTakeSpectrum/Amplitude.

functions.name: GGWave::isDSSEnabled
functions.description: Indicates whether Direct Sequence Spread (DSS) is enabled for this instance.

functions.name: GGWave::samplesPerFrame
functions.description: Returns the number of samples per FFT frame for this instance.

functions.name: GGWave::sampleSizeInp
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of one input sample based on the configured input sample format.

functions.name: GGWave::sampleSizeOut
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of one output sample based on the configured output sample format.

functions.name: GGWave::hzPerSample
functions.description: Returns the frequency resolution (Hz per FFT bin/sample) for the current configuration.

functions.name: GGWave::sampleRateInp
functions.description: Returns the input (capture) sample rate in Hz.

functions.name: GGWave::sampleRateOut
functions.description: Returns the output (playback) sample rate in Hz.

functions.name: GGWave::sampleFormatInp
functions.description: Returns the configured input sample format enumeration.

functions.name: GGWave::sampleFormatOut
functions.description: Returns the configured output sample format enumeration.

functions.name: GGWave::heapSize
functions.description: Returns the total size in bytes of the internal heap allocated by this instance during prepare().

functions.name: GGWave::txWaveform
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the generated waveform buffer from the last encode() call. The data format is determined by sampleFormatOut().
requirements: Call only after a successful encode().
Pointer remains valid as long as the instance remains unchanged and not re-encoded.

functions.name: GGWave::txTones
functions.description: Returns a lightweight view of the tones generated by the last encode() call. Each element is a bin index; -1 separates tones for multi-tone protocols.
requirements: Call only after a successful encode().
Returned ggvector view references internal storage; do not outlive the GGWave instance or subsequent encode operations.

functions.name: GGWave::txHasData
functions.description: Returns true if there is pending data prepared for transmission.

functions.name: GGWave::txTakeAmplitudeI16
functions.description: Consumes and copies the 16-bit amplitude data from the last generated waveform into dst. Returns true if new data was available.
requirements: Call after encode().
dst must be a ggvector<int16_t> wrapper prepared to receive data via its copy/assign semantics (implementation-defined).

functions.name: GGWave::txProtocols
functions.description: Returns the set of TX protocols available to this instance as determined during prepare() based on global Protocols::tx().
requirements: Do not enable protocols here that were not enabled at preparation; comment warns decoding can crash for Rx analog, but for Tx this is read-only.

functions.name: GGWave::rxReceiving
functions.description: Indicates whether the instance is currently in the receiving state (recording frames).

functions.name: GGWave::rxAnalyzing
functions.description: Indicates whether the instance is currently analyzing recorded frames.

functions.name: GGWave::rxSamplesNeeded
functions.description: Returns the number of additional input samples required to proceed in the RX pipeline.

functions.name: GGWave::rxFramesToRecord
functions.description: Returns the total number of frames to record for the current/next RX operation.

functions.name: GGWave::rxFramesLeftToRecord
functions.description: Returns the number of frames left to record in the current RX operation.

functions.name: GGWave::rxFramesToAnalyze
functions.description: Returns the total number of frames that will be analyzed in the RX stage.

functions.name: GGWave::rxFramesLeftToAnalyze
functions.description: Returns the number of frames left to analyze in the current RX stage.

functions.name: GGWave::rxDurationFrames
functions.description: Returns the expected RX duration in frames for the currently selected/active protocol and configuration.

functions.name: GGWave::rxStopReceiving
functions.description: Stops the current RX receiving process if active.

functions.name: GGWave::rxProtocols
functions.description: Returns a mutable reference to the set of RX protocols for this instance. Warning in comments: do not enable protocols here that were not enabled during prepare(), or decoding may crash.
requirements: Only enable protocols that were enabled when the instance was prepared; otherwise decoding may crash (explicit warning in comment).

functions.name: GGWave::rxDataLength
functions.description: Returns the length in bytes of the last successfully received data payload.

functions.name: GGWave::rxData
functions.description: Returns a reference to the buffer containing the last received data payload.
requirements: Reference remains valid until next RX operation that overwrites data or the instance is destroyed.

functions.name: GGWave::rxProtocol
functions.description: Returns a reference to the protocol used for the last successfully decoded payload.

functions.name: GGWave::rxProtocolId
functions.description: Returns a reference to the protocol ID of the last successfully decoded payload.

functions.name: GGWave::rxSpectrum
functions.description: Returns a reference to the last computed RX spectrum.
requirements: Spectrum corresponds to recent RX processing; may change after subsequent decode calls.

functions.name: GGWave::rxAmplitude
functions.description: Returns a reference to the last computed RX amplitude buffer.
requirements: Amplitude corresponds to recent RX processing; may change after subsequent decode calls.

functions.name: GGWave::rxTakeData
functions.description: Consumes the received data by moving/copying it into dst and clearing the internal pending state. Returns the data length in bytes.
requirements: Call after a decode that produced data.
dst must be a ggvector-like wrapper suitable for copy/assign semantics.

functions.name: GGWave::rxTakeSpectrum
functions.description: Consumes the latest spectrum data into dst if available. Returns true if new data was transferred.
requirements: dst must be a ggvector<float>-compatible container wrapper.

functions.name: GGWave::rxTakeAmplitude
functions.description: Consumes the latest amplitude data into dst if available. Returns true if new data was transferred.
requirements: dst must be a ggvector<float>-compatible container wrapper.

functions.name: GGWave::computeFFTR
functions.signature: bool GGWave::computeFFTR(const float * src, float * dst, int N);
functions.description: Computes the FFT of real-valued input src into interleaved complex output dst using the instance’s prepared context. N must equal samplesPerFrame().
requirements: Instance must be prepared.
src must point to N floats; dst must point to 2*N floats.
N must be equal to samplesPerFrame(). Returns false on failure.

functions.name: GGWave::computeFFTR
functions.signature: static int GGWave::computeFFTR(const float * src, float * dst, int N, int * wi, float * wf);
functions.description: Static FFT of real-valued input. Uses/initializes work buffers wi and wf across calls. Returns required sizes when querying, or 1 on success/0 on failure.
requirements: src must point to N floats; dst must point to 2*N floats when performing computation.
First-time call: ensure wi[0] == 0 to initialize internal coefficients.
If wi == nullptr, the return value is the needed size for wi; if wi != nullptr and wf == nullptr, return is needed size for wf; if both non-null, returns 1 on success, 0 on failure.
wf size requirement is 3 + sqrt(N/2) floats (as per comment).

functions.name: GGWave::filter
functions.signature: static int GGWave::filter(ggwave_Filter filter, float * waveform, int N, float p0, float p1, float * w);
functions.description: Applies an in-place filter to the waveform. Initializes internal coefficients into w on first call when w[0]==0 and w[1]==0. For FIRST_ORDER_HIGH_PASS, p0 is cutoff Hz and p1 is sample rate Hz. If w==nullptr, returns required work buffer size; otherwise 1 on success, 0 on failure.
requirements: waveform must point to N floats; filtering is in-place.
On first call per stream, set w[0]==0 and w[1]==0 to trigger initialization.
If w == nullptr, function returns needed size for w for the chosen filter.
For GGWAVE_FILTER_FIRST_ORDER_HIGH_PASS: p0=cutoff frequency in Hz; p1=sample rate in Hz.

functions.name: GGWave::Resampler::Resampler
functions.description: Constructs a Resampler object and initializes internal state. Uses sinc interpolation with a fixed kernel width.

functions.name: GGWave::Resampler::alloc
functions.description: Allocate or bind the internal working buffers of GGWave::Resampler using caller-provided memory. Typical usage in this codebase follows an arena-style pattern: pass a pointer to a contiguous memory block (p) and an integer (n) indicating available bytes; on success the resampler’s internal ggvector buffers are set up to use that memory. If allocation cannot be satisfied, the function returns false. Exact semantics for p == nullptr or how n is updated are not documented in this header and remain unknown.
requirements: p must point to a contiguous, writable memory region large enough to hold the resampler’s internal buffers (exact size unknown; not documented).
n is used as an in/out parameter representing available/remaining bytes; exact update semantics are unknown.
The memory passed via p must remain valid for the lifetime of the resampler’s use of it (until another alloc or object destruction/reset).
Return value: true on successful allocation/setup; false if allocation/setup cannot be performed (inferred from the bool return type and naming pattern).
If p == nullptr behavior is unknown (possibly a size-query pattern); not documented in this header.

functions.name: GGWave::Resampler::reset
functions.description: Resets the resampler internal state (timing and buffers) to initial conditions.

functions.name: GGWave::Resampler::nSamplesTotal
functions.description: Returns the total number of output samples produced so far by the resampler.

functions.name: GGWave::Resampler::resample
functions.signature: int GGWave::Resampler::resample(float factor, int nSamples, const float * samplesInp, float * samplesOut);
functions.description: Resamples nSamples input samples by the given factor using sinc interpolation, writing to samplesOut. Returns the number of output samples produced.
requirements: samplesInp must point to at least nSamples floats.
samplesOut must have enough capacity for the produced samples.
factor is the resampling factor (e.g., out_rate/in_rate); must be positive.
Call alloc/reset appropriately before first use if required by implementation.

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::kDefault
functions.description: Returns a reference to a lazily initialized static default set of protocols, with names, parameters, and enabled flags set for all protocol IDs.
requirements: Returned reference is to static storage; do not free.
Initialization occurs on first call; subsequent calls return the same object.

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::tx
functions.description: Returns the global TX protocols selection (a Protocols object) used to configure instances during prepare().
requirements: Configure (enable/disable/only) before calling GGWave::prepare() to affect new instances.

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::rx
functions.description: Returns the global RX protocols selection (a Protocols object) used to configure instances during prepare().
requirements: Configure (enable/disable/only) before calling GGWave::prepare() to affect new instances.

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::enableAll
functions.description: Enables all protocols in this Protocols set.

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::disableAll
functions.description: Disables all protocols in this Protocols set.

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::toggle
functions.description: Enables or disables a single protocol by ID within this Protocols set.
requirements: id must be within [0, GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_COUNT).

functions.name: GGWave::Protocols::only
functions.description: Disables all protocols except the specified ID within this Protocols set.
requirements: id must be within [0, GGWAVE_PROTOCOL_COUNT).

functions.name: ggvector<T>::assign
functions.description: Assign this ggvector to refer to data from another ggvector. Given operator= is deleted for ggvector, assign likely provides shallow rebinding of the internal pointer/size to match ‘other’ without copying elements. Exact semantics are not documented but are inferred from the class design (pointer/size pair) and the presence of a separate copy() method.
requirements: ‘other’ must refer to valid storage for as long as this ggvector uses it (if assign is a shallow rebind, which is inferred).
No copying of elements is guaranteed by this header; behavior is not explicitly documented.
Sizes are set to match ‘other’; any previous binding of this ggvector is overwritten (inferred).

functions.name: ggvector<T>::copy
functions.description: Copy elements from another ggvector into this ggvector’s storage. This is likely a deep copy of element values into the memory pointed to by this ggvector, contrasting with assign(). Exact behavior is not documented; inference is based on the method name and the class design.
requirements: This ggvector must already reference writable storage (data() != nullptr) with size() >= other.size() to avoid overruns (inferred).
Element type T must be copyable (inferred).
If sizes do not match, behavior is unspecified in this header; callers should ensure capacity suffices.

functions.name: ggvector<T>::zero
functions.description: Sets all elements in the wrapped range to zero.
requirements: Underlying buffer must be valid and size() known.

functions.name: ggvector<T>::zero
functions.description: Sets the first n elements in the wrapped range to zero.
requirements: Underlying buffer must be valid.

functions.name: ggmatrix<T>::zero
functions.description: Zero-initializes all elements of the 2D matrix view.
requirements: Underlying buffer must be valid and sizes set.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Generator for GGWave text/binary payloads used by Tx init paths.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for both:
#  - text: expects UTF-8 bytes and the stub appends a terminating NUL
#  - binary: arbitrary bytes; size capped to GGWave::kMaxDataSize (256)
#
# Strategy:
#  - Produce valid UTF-8 strings that cover a variety of code point ranges
#    (ASCII, Latin-1 supplement, BMP including combining marks, emoji).
#  - Randomly include edge-case patterns: empty, short, max-length, repeated chars,
#    mixed scripts, right-to-left marks, null-free to keep validity before stub adds NUL.
#  - Sometimes return bytes that look random but still valid UTF-8 by construction.
#  - Keep length <= 256 to respect kMaxDataSize when used as binary.
#
# The fuzzer framework will deserialize this single bytes buffer for FUZZ_PARAM_STR and
# potentially reuse or slice it. We ensure the output is valid UTF-8 and interesting.

ASCII = [chr(i) for i in range(0x20, 0x7F)]  # printable ASCII
WHITESPACE = [" ", "\t", "\n"]
LATIN1 = [chr(i) for i in range(0x00A1, 0x00FF + 1)]
COMBINING = [
    "\u0300", "\u0301", "\u0302", "\u0303", "\u0308", "\u0327", "\u030A", "\u0308", "\u034F"
]
CJK = [
    chr(i) for i in (
        list(range(0x4E00, 0x4E10)) +  # a few CJK ideographs
        list(range(0x3040, 0x3048)) +  # Hiragana
        list(range(0x30A0, 0x30A8))    # Katakana
    )
]
EMOJI = [
    "\U0001F600", "\U0001F601", "\U0001F602", "\U0001F603", "\U0001F604",
    "\U0001F680", "\U0001F4A9", "\U0001F984", "\U0001F44D", "\U0001F9E9"
]
RTL_MARKS = ["\u200F", "\u202E", "\u202B", "\u2067", "\u2069"]  # RLM, RLO, RLE, RLI, PDI
PUNCT = list("-_.:,;!?/\\|()[]{}'\"@#%&*+")

# Build pools for varied composition
POOL_BASIC = ASCII + WHITESPACE + PUNCT
POOL_EXT = LATIN1 + CJK + EMOJI

MAX_SIZE = 256  # GGWave::kMaxDataSize


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, items: List[str]) -> str:
    return items[rng.randrange(0, len(items))]


def _make_ascii_chunk(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Dense ASCII with occasional whitespace/punct
    chars = []
    for _ in range(n):
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            chars.append(_rand_choice(rng, WHITESPACE))
        elif rng.random() < 0.20:
            chars.append(_rand_choice(rng, PUNCT))
        else:
            chars.append(_rand_choice(rng, ASCII))
    return "".join(chars)


def _make_unicode_chunk(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> str:
    # Mix from extended pools, insert combining marks occasionally
    pieces = []
    for _ in range(n):
        r = rng.random()
        if r < 0.45:
            pieces.append(_rand_choice(rng, LATIN1))
        elif r < 0.75:
            pieces.append(_rand_choice(rng, CJK))
        else:
            pieces.append(_rand_choice(rng, EMOJI))
        if rng.random() < 0.15:
            # add 1-2 combining marks after a base character
            pieces.append(_rand_choice(rng, COMBINING))
            if rng.random() < 0.3:
                pieces.append(_rand_choice(rng, COMBINING))
    return "".join(pieces)


def _make_structured_text(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> str:
    # Create strings like URLs, key=value pairs, JSON-like, CSV-like
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        # URL-like
        host = _make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(3, 10)).replace(" ", "").lower()
        path = _make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, 10)).replace(" ", "")
        s = f"https://{host}.example.com/{path}"
    elif choice == 1:
        # key=value;value2...
        keys = ["mode", "proto", "rate", "volume", "sr", "fmt"]
        parts = []
        for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 6)):
            k = rng.choice(keys)
            if k in ("mode", "fmt"):
                v = _rand_choice(rng, ["tx", "rx", "i16", "f32", "u8"])  # symbolic
            elif k in ("proto",):
                v = str(rng.randrange(0, 16))
            elif k in ("rate", "sr"):
                v = str(rng.choice([8000, 11025, 16000, 22050, 32000, 44100, 48000]))
            elif k == "volume":
                v = str(rng.randrange(0, 101))
            parts.append(f"{k}={v}")
        s = ";".join(parts)
    elif choice == 2:
        # JSON-like (not necessarily strict JSON but UTF-8 safe)
        keychars = string.ascii_letters
        kv = []
        for _ in range(rng.randrange(2, 6)):
            k = ''.join(rng.choice(keychars) for _ in range(rng.randrange(3, 8)))
            v = _make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, 6))
            kv.append(f'"{k}":"{v}"')
        s = "{" + ",".join(kv) + "}"
    else:
        # CSV-like with mixed unicode fields
        fields = []
        for _ in range(rng.randrange(3, 8)):
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                fields.append(_make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, 8)))
            else:
                fields.append(_make_unicode_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(1, 4)))
        s = ",".join(fields)
    # Enforce budget in bytes while keeping valid UTF-8 by slicing on code points
    # Python slicing is code point aware, so encode after trimming.
    while len(s.encode('utf-8')) > budget and len(s) > 0:
        s = s[:-1]
    return s


def _compose_text(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a pattern for maximum variety
    # Ensure output <= MAX_SIZE bytes when encoded
    budget = rng.randrange(0, MAX_SIZE + 1)  # allow empty up to 256 bytes

    mode = rng.randrange(0, 8)
    if mode == 0:
        s = _make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, min(64, budget + 1)))
    elif mode == 1:
        s = _make_unicode_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, max(1, budget // 2 + 1)))
    elif mode == 2:
        s = _make_structured_text(rng, budget)
    elif mode == 3:
        # Repetitive patterns that may influence tone structure
        token = rng.choice(["A", "0", "~", "GGWAVE", "DATA"]) + ("\u0301" if rng.random() < 0.3 else "")
        reps = max(0, budget // max(1, len(token.encode('utf-8'))))
        reps = min(reps, rng.randrange(0, 40))
        s = token * reps
    elif mode == 4:
        # Mixed scripts paragraph
        parts = []
        while True:
            choice = rng.random()
            if choice < 0.4:
                parts.append(_make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, 10)))
            elif choice < 0.8:
                parts.append(_make_unicode_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(1, 5)))
            else:
                parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, RTL_MARKS))
            candidate = " ".join(p for p in parts if p is not None)
            if len(candidate.encode('utf-8')) > budget:
                parts = parts[:-1]
                break
            if len(parts) > rng.randrange(3, 8):
                break
        s = " ".join(parts)
    elif mode == 5:
        # Numeric payload, useful for binary-like data
        nums = [str(rng.randrange(0, 256)) for _ in range(rng.randrange(1, 40))]
        s = ",".join(nums)
        while len(s.encode('utf-8')) > budget and len(nums) > 0:
            nums.pop()
            s = ",".join(nums)
    elif mode == 6:
        # Short emoji sequence
        count = rng.randrange(0, min(10, budget // 4 + 1))
        s = "".join(rng.choice(EMOJI) for _ in range(count))
    else:
        # Mixed bag
        s = _make_ascii_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, budget // 2 + 1)) + _make_unicode_chunk(rng, rng.randrange(0, 8))
        while len(s.encode('utf-8')) > budget and len(s) > 0:
            s = s[:-1]

    # Ensure we don't include embedded NULs; stub adds NUL itself
    s = s.replace("\x00", "")

    # Occasionally craft extreme sizes exactly 0 or MAX_SIZE
    r = rng.random()
    if r < 0.05:
        s = ""
    elif r < 0.10:
        # Fill to MAX_SIZE bytes with safe ASCII
        base = _make_ascii_chunk(rng, 32)
        # Repeat to reach budget = MAX_SIZE
        target = MAX_SIZE
        out = []
        while len("".join(out).encode('utf-8')) + len(base.encode('utf-8')) <= target:
            out.append(base)
        s = ("".join(out))[:target]  # slicing on characters; ensure <= target bytes below
        while len(s.encode('utf-8')) > target:
            s = s[:-1]

    return s


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose to bias toward valid UTF-8 human-readable text, but all valid UTF-8.
    s = _compose_text(rng)

    # As the fuzz stubs may use the same FUZZ_PARAM_STR for binary path as well,
    # we sometimes ensure dense byte coverage while keeping valid UTF-8 by wrapping
    # ASCII with non-ASCII code points that expand encoding sizes.
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and len(s.encode('utf-8')) < MAX_SIZE:
        # Pad with a variety of code points to reach a more interesting size
        pad = []
        while len((s + "".join(pad)).encode('utf-8')) < MAX_SIZE and len(pad) < 16:
            pad.append(_rand_choice(rng, EMOJI + LATIN1 + CJK))
        candidate = s + "".join(pad)
        # Trim to MAX_SIZE bytes boundary without breaking code points
        while len(candidate.encode('utf-8')) > MAX_SIZE and len(candidate) > 0:
            candidate = candidate[:-1]
        s = candidate

    # Encode to UTF-8 bytes; ensure size <= 256 bytes
    data = s.encode('utf-8')
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        # Safe trim by code points already enforced, but keep guard
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
        # Ensure we did not split a code point: back off to a valid boundary
        while True:
            try:
                _ = data.decode('utf-8')
                break
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                data = data[:-1]

    return data
